prompt.context_jp: 初冬の午後、五月の携帯＿短く震えた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 初冬の午後、五月の携帯＿短く震えた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that fits the narrative opening.

feedback.correct_en: The phone vibrating is brand-new information introducing the scene — が marks this newly-appearing event.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would mark 'the phone' as an already-established topic, but here it's the first mention introducing the action.

contrast_examples.jp: その電話は彼女のだった。
contrast_examples.en: That phone was hers. (topic already known)

prompt.context_jp: 「声＿変だねえ ケイちゃんの番号と違ってるし」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle: she's noticing something odd right now.

feedback.correct_en: She's reporting a newly-noticed observation ('the voice is strange') — が marks this fresh perception.
feedback.incorrect_en: 声は変だ would sound like contrasting the voice with something else, which doesn't fit the suspicious discovery here.

contrast_examples.jp: 声は変だけど、話し方は似てる。
contrast_examples.en: The voice is off, but the speech pattern is similar. (contrast)

prompt.context_jp: 「女の人＿ 俺の手つかんで…」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「女の人＿ 俺の手つかんで…」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle introducing a new character in the story.

feedback.correct_en: The woman is being introduced for the first time as the agent of a sudden action — が marks new-information subjects.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would treat 'the woman' as a known topic, but she has just appeared in the narrative.

contrast_examples.jp: 女の人が手をつかんだ。
あの女の人は知り合いだ。
contrast_examples.en: That woman is an acquaintance. (known topic)

prompt.context_jp: ケイちゃんが そんなこと するような子じゃないっていうのは 母さん＿ いちばん よく分かってるから！
prompt.prompt_jp: 母さん＿ いちばん よく分かってる
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle: 'Mom knows best.'

feedback.correct_en: In 'X-が一番よく分かってる' structures, が exhaustively identifies WHO knows best — Mom, more than anyone.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make it a general topic comment, losing the 'it's Mom who knows best (not anyone else)' exhaustive sense.

contrast_examples.jp: 母さんが一番分かってる。
contrast_examples.en: Mom is the one who understands best.

prompt.context_jp: 示談金という言葉が並び、母親の動揺を煽って財布を開かせる筋書き＿透けて見えた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for the narrator's sudden realization.

feedback.correct_en: The scheme becoming visible is new information perceived by May — が marks the newly-appearing subject of 透けて見えた.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would treat 'the scheme' as an established topic, but it's being noticed here for the first time.

prompt.context_jp: 五月は震える母親＿演じ切りながら…
prompt.prompt_jp: 震える母親＿演じ切りながら
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking what she is playing.

feedback.correct_en: 演じる takes a direct object (the role being played), marked by を.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark subject, に would mark direction/target — neither fits the verb 演じる's object.

prompt.context_jp: 本当に この世を 動かしているの＿ 実は 影の黒子たちだ
prompt.prompt_jp: この世を動かしているの＿ 影の黒子たちだ
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle: 'The ones who move the world ARE the shadow operators.'

feedback.correct_en: The cleft 'Xの は Yだ' names what X is — は topicalizes the whole 'the ones moving the world' clause and equates it with 影の黒子たち.
feedback.incorrect_en: が here would sound like identifying new information rather than fitting the rhetorical 'what truly moves the world IS...' topic–comment frame.

contrast_examples.jp: 動かしているのは彼らだ。
contrast_examples.en: The ones moving it are them. (topic-comment identification)

prompt.context_jp: 若い男に指示を飛ばす兄貴分＿、金の受け取りを何より急いでいる。
prompt.prompt_jp: 兄貴分＿、金の受け取りを何より急いでいる。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle establishing the older brother as topic.

feedback.correct_en: The sentence makes a characterizing comment about the already-introduced boss figure — は sets him as the topic.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would signal new-information identification, but this sentence is describing a known character's state/behavior.

contrast_examples.en: The boss is in a hurry. (topic comment)

contrast_examples.jp: 誰が急いでいるの？—兄貴分が。
contrast_examples.en: Who is in a hurry? — The boss. (exhaustive answer)

prompt.context_jp: 「おい 弁護士＿ 金取りに行くから そこで待ってろって電話しろ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「弁護士＿ 金取りに行くから…」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle: the boss announces an upcoming action.

feedback.correct_en: The lawyer coming to collect money is new information being delivered as a reason — が marks the subject of this newly-reported event.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would frame 'the lawyer' as an established topic, but he's being announced as the agent of a new action.

contrast_examples.jp: 弁護士が行くから待て。
contrast_examples.en: A lawyer is going, so wait.
The lawyer has already gone home. (known topic)

prompt.context_jp: 「あっ… 電話 鳴ってますよ」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle (implied): she points out that a phone is ringing right now.

feedback.correct_en: Pointing out a sudden sensory event ('the phone is ringing!') uses が for the new-information subject.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make it sound like a general statement about the phone, not an urgent live observation.

prompt.context_jp: 男の視線＿、握りしめた封筒に落ちる。
prompt.prompt_jp: 男の視線＿、封筒に落ちる。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle: a narrative description of a sudden action.

feedback.correct_en: Narrative descriptions of a single observable action use が to present the subject as part of the scene.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would treat 視線 as topic, giving a general statement rather than the vivid cinematic 'his gaze falls on...'.

prompt.context_jp: 「鈴木二葉君 今日から 君＿秘書室長だ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「今日から 君＿秘書室長だ」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle: the president appoints her.

feedback.correct_en: Announcing 'YOU are the one who will be the head' — が exhaustively identifies her as the appointee.
feedback.incorrect_en: 君は秘書室長だ would sound more like a casual topic statement; appointments use が to single out the person.

prompt.context_jp: 「派遣社員の望月さんのほう＿ よっぽど分かってるじゃない」
prompt.prompt_jp: 望月さんのほう＿ よっぽど分かってる
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle: contrasting Mochizuki against Terui.

feedback.correct_en: 'Xのほうが〜' is the fixed comparative structure — が marks the item that scores higher in the comparison.
feedback.incorrect_en: は wouldn't fit the 〜のほうが pattern used to say 'X more so than Y'.

prompt.context_jp: 「私も家内も うなぎより ご飯の量が多い “梅”＿好きなんだよ」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle expressing the president's personal preference.

feedback.correct_en: 好きだ is a stative adjective — the thing liked is marked by が, not を.
feedback.incorrect_en: を marks direct objects of action verbs; 好き is not an action verb, so を is ungrammatical here.

prompt.context_jp: 「千代さんの銀行＿ ＳＮＳで盛り上がってます」
prompt.prompt_jp: 千代さんの銀行＿ ＳＮＳで盛り上がってます
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle alerting Chiyo to a new buzz.

feedback.correct_en: She's reporting a newly-noticed fact — the bank's trending now — so が marks this new-information subject.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would treat the bank as a topic of ongoing discussion, missing the 'look, this just happened' flavor.

contrast_examples.jp: ニュースが盛り上がってる。
contrast_examples.en: The news is blowing up (just noticed).

prompt.context_jp: 「パワハラなら訴えられるけど それよりタチ＿悪い」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle in the fixed phrase 'タチ＿悪い'.

feedback.correct_en: タチが悪い is a set collocation ('it's a nasty kind') where the quality is marked with が.
feedback.incorrect_en: タチは悪い is not the idiomatic form; the fixed phrase uses が inside the predicate.

contrast_examples.en: That guy is a nasty type.

prompt.context_jp: 「照井さん 手＿空いてるなら 手伝ってもらえますか？」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle in the fixed phrase 'free/available'.

feedback.correct_en: 手が空く ('to be free/available') is a set phrase where 手 is marked with が within the predicate.
feedback.incorrect_en: 手は空いてる would awkwardly topicalize 'hands' as if contrasting with something else, breaking the idiom.

prompt.context_jp: 「被害者の女性が示談にしてもいいと ＿＿＿＿＿まして…」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the honorific speech verb the fake lawyer uses.

feedback.correct_en: おっしゃる is the honorific (sonkeigo) form of 言う, used to elevate the victim's words.
feedback.incorrect_en: 申す is humble (used for oneself); いたす is a humble do-verb, neither fits reporting what the other party said.

contrast_examples.jp: 先生がおっしゃいました。

prompt.context_jp: 「私から お金を ＿＿＿＿＿取ろうとしてる…」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb meaning 'to swindle/cheat out of'.

feedback.correct_en: ダマし取る ('to swindle/trick out of') is the exact collocation for scam-victim framing.
feedback.incorrect_en: 受け取る means simply 'receive'; 引き取る means 'collect/take away' — neither conveys the deception.

prompt.context_jp: 「＿＿＿＿＿ほどの者ではございません」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「＿＿＿＿＿ほどの者ではございません」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb for 'not worth announcing myself'.

feedback.correct_en: 名乗るほどの者ではない is a stock humble phrase: 'I'm not someone worthy of giving my name.'
feedback.incorrect_en: 呼ぶ (to call) and 語る (to narrate) don't form this idiomatic self-effacing expression.

contrast_examples.jp: 名乗るほどの者ではない。

prompt.context_jp: 「お昼は うなぎを ＿＿＿＿＿たいと…」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the honorific verb for 'the president wants to eat'.

feedback.correct_en: 召し上がる is the honorific (sonkeigo) form of 食べる, used for the superior (president).
feedback.incorrect_en: いただく is humble (for oneself); 食べる is plain and improper when referring to the boss's action.

prompt.context_jp: 「これからは 私に何でも じかに ＿＿＿＿＿くださいませ」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the humble-honorific verb for 'please tell me (directly)'.

feedback.correct_en: お申しつけください is the set honorific for 'please instruct/order me' used when accepting commands from a superior.
feedback.incorrect_en: おっしゃってください is general 'please say'; お伝えしてください wrongly mixes humble form — neither fits this subservient 'order me anything' nuance.

contrast_examples.jp: 何なりとお申しつけください。
ご遠慮なくおっしゃってください。

prompt.context_jp: 「あのお金 ＿＿＿＿＿すれば み～んな 萬さんに 借金 返せたのに」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the slang verb meaning 'pocket/keep illicitly'.

feedback.correct_en: ネコババする means to secretly pocket something that isn't yours — exactly what Fujiko jokes about.
feedback.incorrect_en: 山分け is 'split evenly'; 仕分け is 'sort' — neither captures the illicit 'keep for yourself' nuance.

contrast_examples.jp: 落とし物をネコババする。

prompt.context_jp: 「室長の 無視カゴに ＿＿＿＿＿ますよ」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the passive form: 'you'll get put into the ignore basket'.

feedback.correct_en: 入れられる is the passive — 'to be put in' by someone else (the director), fitting the victim's perspective.
feedback.incorrect_en: 入って is intransitive ('enter by oneself'); 入れて is causative/active without passive — neither captures being targeted.

contrast_examples.jp: ブラックリストに入れられる。
contrast_examples.en: To be put on the blacklist.

prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word for 'it gives me the creeps'.

feedback.correct_en: 虫酸が走る is a set idiom meaning 'it makes my skin crawl' out of disgust — the right fit for revulsion at sycophants.
feedback.incorrect_en: 寒気がする ('feel chills') and 鳥肌が立つ ('get goosebumps') exist but don't carry the specifically disgusted connotation of 虫酸が走る.

prompt.context_jp: 室長から仕事を指示されたとき、秘書が返す言葉として自然なのは？
prompt.prompt_en: Which response is natural when a secretary receives an instruction from the director?

feedback.correct_en: かしこまりました is the standard business/secretarial acknowledgment to a superior's order.
feedback.incorrect_en: わかったよ is casual and would be rude from a secretary speaking to her director.

contrast_examples.jp: かしこまりました、すぐに対応します。
わかったよ、やっとくね。
contrast_examples.en: Got it, I'll do it. (casual, among friends)

prompt.context_jp: 頭取の奥さまに初めて会ったとき、秘書の挨拶として自然なのは？
prompt.prompt_en: Which greeting is natural when a secretary meets the president's wife for the first time?

choices.text: お初に お目にかかります。
初めて 会えて うれしいです。

feedback.correct_en: お目にかかる is the humble form of 会う used in formal first meetings with superiors — the expected business phrase.
feedback.incorrect_en: 初めて会えてうれしいです is natural between peers but too casual for greeting the boss's wife in a corporate setting.

contrast_examples.jp: お初にお目にかかります。

prompt.context_jp: 秘書室長が会議で権限を主張する言い方として自然なのは？
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing sounds natural for a director asserting authority in a meeting?

choices.text: 今後は全て 秘書室長の私を通していただきます。
これから全部 私に通してもらうから。

feedback.correct_en: 〜ていただきます with the title name reinforces her authority in a formal business meeting — matches the drama's tone.
feedback.incorrect_en: もらうから is too plain/blunt for a formal corporate meeting setting among executives.

prompt.context_jp: 落ち込んでいる七菜に向けて、萬さんが言う言葉として自然なのは？
prompt.prompt_en: Which encouragement sounds most natural coming from the gruff ramen shop master?

choices.text: 腹いっぱい食べて寝れば 大概のことは なんとかなる。
お腹をたくさん食べて寝たら ほとんどのことは解決します。

feedback.correct_en: 腹いっぱい and 大概のことはなんとかなる are idiomatic, warm, blunt expressions suiting Man's gruff-but-caring voice.
feedback.incorrect_en: お腹をたくさん食べる is unnatural collocation (you don't 'eat your stomach'); the phrasing feels stiff and textbook-like.

contrast_examples.en: Eat a lot. (also natural but less flavorful)

prompt.context_jp: 刑事ドラマの取調室らしいセリフとして自然なのは？
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds like a classic interrogation-room trope in Japanese drama?

choices.text: まあ カツ丼でも食べてから。
では 先に食事を済ませましょう。

feedback.correct_en: カツ丼でも食べてから is the iconic interrogation-room cliché — 'でも' softens and the katsudon reference is cultural shorthand.
feedback.incorrect_en: The second line is grammatically fine but generic and misses the famous trope-flavor the scene is riffing on.

contrast_examples.en: Want some tea or something? (casual suggestion)
Let's drink tea. (plain polite, no softness)
